parameters.label: Średnica impaktora (założenie modelu Range 2022)
parameters.locator: Sec. 2.1; asteroid.inp (OBJRESH=70 cells x 100 m radius)
parameters.notes: Chosen to match crater-structure simulations (Collins et al. 2008; Morgan et al. 2016 as cited). Input, not a result.

parameters.label: Gęstość impaktora (założenie)
parameters.notes: Granite-like projectile in iSALE (OBJMAT granite).

parameters.label: Prędkość uderzenia (założenie)
Kąt uderzenia w modelu (pionowy)
parameters.notes: Vertical impact forced by 2-D axisymmetric iSALE. Collins et al. 2020 infer 45-60 deg from horizontal, from the NE. Range et al. expect a slightly larger rim wave downrange and smaller uprange (not quantified).

parameters.label: Głębokość oceanu w modelu hydrokodu (fiducial)
parameters.notes: Constant depth (axisymmetry). 1, 2, 3 km tested; rim wave/crater 'do not depend strongly' on depth within 1-3 km; authors warn this need not hold for much shallower water.

parameters.label: Grubość warstwy osadów nad granitem (model)
parameters.notes: Target: granitic crust + 4 km sediments (calcite in input file) + water.

parameters.label: Rozdzielczość siatki hydrokodu iSALE
parameters.notes: 2500 x 600 high-resolution cells; high-res zone 250 km; mesh 0-344.3 km horizontal; 200 m test gives similar waveform.

parameters.label: Czas przekazania hydrokod -> model płytkowodny
parameters.notes: 850 s hand-off tested: nearly identical global energies.

parameters.label: Rozdzielczość globalnego modelu płytkowodnego (MOM6/MOST)
parameters.notes: 1/5 deg test similar. MOM6 dt 10 s, MOST dt 6 s; domain 86.05S-82.05N. Arrival times stated accurate to ~1% at 1/10 deg (MOM6).

parameters.label: Czas symulacji globalnej
parameters.notes: No runup/inundation modelled (1/10 deg too coarse).

parameters.label: Energia kinetyczna impaktora w scenariuszu Range 2022
parameters.notes: Consistent with 0.5*m*v^2 for 14 km, 2650 kg/m3, 12 km/s. Sanford et al. 2016 (Sec. 1) cite 4.2-12e23 J from older literature; scenario-dependent.

parameters.label: Wysokość ściany wody pchanej kurtyną ejekty (t=2,5 min)
parameters.notes: Ejecta-curtain-driven water wall at ~70-80 km radius (read from Fig. 1a); not yet a freely propagating tsunami.

parameters.label: Amplituda fali brzeżnej (rim wave) w chwili przekazania (10 min)
parameters.notes: 1.5 km in main text; SI gives 1.4 km at 600 s (fiducial) and 1.2 km when ejecta leaving a 50 km-high mesh are removed. Height above resting sea level; most wave breaking ends before 600 s.

parameters.label: Odległość czoła fali brzeżnej od punktu uderzenia (10 min)
parameters.notes: Fig. 2: positive hump ~155-245 km, crest ~220-230 km; sea surface depressed (-0.3 to -0.7 km) between ~70 and 150 km (water returning to crater).

parameters.label: Długość fali brzeżnej
parameters.notes: Stated as 'about 50-100 km'; 75 is the midpoint for convenience. Wavelength >> depth, so shallow-water approximation applies after hand-off.

parameters.label: Ile razy mniej energii ma fala samego zapadania krateru (bez rim wave), po 4 h
parameters.notes: Supports rim-wave dominance (agreeing with Wunnemann & Weiss 2015 as cited). Contrasts with matsui2002.

parameters.label: Deficyt energii wariantu 'Half Crater' vs 'Full Crater'
parameters.notes: About 5% less energy when the crater portion over pre-impact land is kept as land (fiducial).

parameters.label: Prędkość czoła fali na głębokim oceanie
parameters.notes: 'in excess of 200 m/s in deep water, in accordance with the shallow-water celerity' (sqrt(9.81*4000 m) = 198 m/s).

parameters.label: Promień czoła fali po 1 h (Zatoka Meksykańska)
parameters.notes: Leading ring at ~700-830 km from the impact point in paleo-coordinates; implies ~177 m/s mean between 600 s (220 km) and 1 h.

parameters.label: Zasięg czoła fali na wschód po 4 h
parameters.notes: Eastward front ~27 deg of longitude from impact at ~20N paleolatitude; southward only ~1600 km. Approximate figure reading.

parameters.label: Wejście fali z Zatoki do Atlantyku
parameters.notes: 'spread outside the Gulf into the Atlantic after about 1 hr from impact'. In the Range paleogeography the Gulf opens broadly to the east.

parameters.label: Wejście fali do Pacyfiku przez cieśninę środkowoamerykańską
parameters.notes: 'after 4 hr, through the Central American seaway, the waves enter into the Pacific'. Depends on assumed open, deep seaway in the paleobathymetry.

parameters.label: Przejście fali przez większość Atlantyku (od zachodu)
parameters.notes: Upper bound: state at 24 h post-hand-off (=24 h + 600 s). Waves 'cross most of the Pacific from the east and Atlantic from the west'.

parameters.label: Wejście fali do Oceanu Indyjskiego (z obu stron)
parameters.notes: Upper bound (24 h post-hand-off snapshot).

parameters.label: Znaczące amplitudy na większości wybrzeży świata
parameters.notes: 48 h post-hand-off; complex pattern from reflection/refraction. Beyond the 24 h window (context).

parameters.label: Wysokość fali na otwartych wodach Zatoki Meksykańskiej
parameters.notes: 'generally higher than 100 m' (lower bound). Fig. 4a colour scale saturated (>=10 m) everywhere in the Gulf.

parameters.label: Wysokość fali w północnej Zatoce po 1 h (przy krawędzi szelfu)
parameters.locator: kinsland2025 Sec. 'Computer models and tsunami characteristics'; range2022 Fig. 3a (scale +/-500 m)
parameters.notes: 'perhaps 400-500 m after one hour of propagation of the rim wave, when the wave would have been approaching the paleoshelf break'.

parameters.label: Wysokość fali w północnej Zatoce po 4 h (po przejściu szelfu)
parameters.locator: kinsland2025 same section; range2022 Fig. 3b (scale +/-50 m)
parameters.notes: '40-50 m after 4 h when the tsunami would have already crossed the paleoshelf'.

parameters.label: Maks. wysokość fali na otwartym Północnym Atlantyku
parameters.locator: Fig. 4a (read from colour scale); Sec. 3.2; Plain Language Summary
parameters.notes: Western/central N Atlantic saturated at >=10 m (scale caps at 1000 cm); eastern N Atlantic ~2-8 m. Text: 'over 10 m offshore amplitudes' along many N Atlantic coasts.

parameters.label: Maks. wysokość fali na Południowym Pacyfiku (wiązka przez CAS)
parameters.notes: Directed beam from the Central American Seaway toward the SW Pacific: 600-800 cm contours, locally saturated near coasts.

parameters.label: Maks. wysokość fali na Północnym Pacyfiku
parameters.notes: Mostly 1-2 m (200 cm contours).

parameters.label: Maks. wysokość fali na Południowym Atlantyku
parameters.notes: Largely shielded; equatorial S Atlantic higher (flow >20 cm/s there per abstract).

parameters.label: Maks. wysokość fali na Oceanie Indyjskim
parameters.notes: Lowest colour class (<~1 m); 'with the exception of some coasts along the Indian Ocean and Mediterranean' near-shore amplitudes exceed 1 m.

parameters.label: Maks. wysokość fali w Tetydzie / basenie śródziemnomorskim
parameters.notes: Approximate; consistent with complete K-Pg sections around Mediterranean.

parameters.label: Amplituda przybrzeżna (offshore) na świecie - dolna granica
parameters.notes: 'around the world near-shore amplitudes exceed 1 m', except some Indian Ocean and Mediterranean coasts. Runup not modelled; shoaling would amplify.

parameters.label: Amplituda przy wybrzeżach Płn. Atlantyku i Płd. Pacyfiku
parameters.notes: 'over 10 m' offshore amplitude (lower bound) along many N Atlantic and some S American Pacific coasts.

parameters.label: Prędkość przepływu wody w pobliżu krateru
parameters.notes: 'exceeds 100 m/s' (lower bound).

parameters.label: Prędkość przepływu przy wybrzeżach Płn. Atlantyku/Płd. Pacyfiku
parameters.notes: 'in excess of 1 m/s offshore' (lower bound).

parameters.label: Maks. prędkość przepływu (uśredniona w słupie wody) - otwarty Płn. Atlantyk
parameters.notes: Depth-averaged velocity (shallow-water model), not true near-bed velocity. ~40-80 cm/s in central N Atlantic.

parameters.label: Maks. prędkość przepływu - Płd. Pacyfik
parameters.notes: ~20-60 cm/s along the beam; >20 cm/s more than 12,000 km from impact.

parameters.label: Maks. prędkość przepływu - Płn. Pacyfik i Ocean Indyjski
parameters.notes: Below the 20 cm/s contour over most open-ocean areas.

parameters.label: Próg prędkości erozji drobnych osadów pelagicznych
parameters.method: empirical threshold cited by range2022 (Lonsdale & Southard 1974; McCave 1984)
parameters.notes: Second-hand: the primary sediment-transport papers were not opened in this thread.

parameters.label: Zasięg obszarów z prędkością >20 cm/s (potencjalna erozja dna)
parameters.locator: Abstract (>10,000 km); Sec. 3.2 and 4.2 (>12,000 km, New Zealand)

parameters.label: Całkowita energia tsunami (kinetyczna+potencjalna) na starcie
parameters.locator: Table S4 (Full Crater, with Rim Wave, 600 s, 'max'); Fig. S4
parameters.notes: Fig. S4 caption states 5.1e19 J for the fiducial run, but Table S4 ratio (0.19% of 2.7e23 J), the '30,000x' claim (5.1e20/1.7e16) and the Fig. S4 ratio curve (~2.5e4 at 1 h) all imply ~5e20 J; the caption value is most likely a typo (flagged, not resolved).

parameters.label: Energia tsunami 4 h po przekazaniu (Half Crater)
parameters.notes: MOM6 3.90e19 J, MOST 3.84e19 J: model-independent. Decay ~13x from hand-off ('Van Dorn effect': faster dissipation of explosion/impact waves).

parameters.label: Stosunek energii tsunami Chicxulub do tsunami 2004 (maks.)
parameters.notes: 'up to 30,000 times'. Ratio falls with time (~2.5e4 at 1 h to ~3e3 at 7 h of ocean simulation, Fig. S4) because the impact tsunami dissipates faster.

parameters.label: Energia tsunami 2004 (Ocean Indyjski) - porównanie
parameters.method: model (Smith et al. 2005 HIM run; Tang et al. 2012) as cited by range2022
parameters.notes: 9.1e15 J four hours later. Second-hand citation.

parameters.label: Energia tsunami Tohoku 2011 - porównanie
parameters.method: DART-based estimate (Tang et al. 2012) as cited by range2022
parameters.notes: 1.5e15 J four hours later. Second-hand citation.

parameters.label: Amplituda offshore tsunami 2004 po 2 h (dla porównania)
parameters.method: measured (satellite altimetry, Smith et al. 2005) as cited by range2022
parameters.notes: Second-hand citation; context for scale.

parameters.label: Sprawność zamiany energii uderzenia na energię tsunami
parameters.notes: 0.19%; earthquake tsunamis average ~0.1% (0.02-0.8%, Tang et al. 2012 as cited). Can be used to scale tsunami energy if the reference scenario's impact energy differs (assumes same efficiency - extrapolation).

parameters.label: Możliwe zawyżenie amplitud przez model płytkowodny (brak dyspersji)
parameters.method: literature estimate cited by range2022 (Son et al. 2011; Zhou et al. 2012, 2014)
parameters.notes: 'up to 50% of amplitudes in certain cases'; shallow-water results treated as conservative (upper-bound) amplitudes. Far-field pattern expected to change little.

parameters.label: Odsetek niekompletnych profili K-Pg w strefach modelowanego przepływu >20 cm/s
parameters.notes: Correlation, not proof: hiatuses on bathymetric highs can have other causes (bottom currents, slope failure, drilling strategy), discussed in Sec. 5.2.

parameters.label: Odsetek kompletnych profili K-Pg w strefach przepływu <20 cm/s (dolna granica)
parameters.notes: 'At least 65%'. Same caveat as above.

parameters.label: Średnica impaktora (założenie Matsui 2002)
parameters.method: model:matsui2002 (input, Ir-based estimate of Alvarez et al. 1980)
parameters.notes: Energy assumed 1e8-1e9 Mt TNT; crater diameter 180 km; crater shape taken as present-day structure.

parameters.label: Głębokość wody na platformie Jukatanu (założenie Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: Controls the crater-generated wave: with 100 m depth max water level in crater falls to 40% and wave energy to ~17% of the 200 m case.

parameters.label: Rozdzielczość siatki modelu Matsui 2002
parameters.notes: Nonlinear long-wave theory (leap-frog/upwind), 2-layer landslide model, domain Gulf of Mexico + Caribbean, paleogeography after Ross & Scotese 1988.

parameters.label: Amplituda fali brzeżnej na krawędzi platformy (Matsui 2002)
parameters.method: scaling: Gault & Sonett 1982 lab experiments + breaking criterion (amplitude ~ shelf depth), 1/r decay
parameters.locator: p. 73 'Behavior of the rim wave'; Fig. 3
parameters.notes: 'several meters' in deep water 500 km away; concluded the rim wave dispersed quickly ('No measurable wave was found ahead of the receding wave'). Order-of-magnitude estimate, not a hydrocode result.

parameters.label: Wysokość fali wychodzącej z krateru na jego krawędzi (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: For a 200 m platform depth.

parameters.label: Okres fali generowanej przez krater (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: Long period because inflow over a shallow platform is slow.

parameters.label: Czas wypełnienia krateru wodą (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: Contrasts with 30-60 min to flood up to the peak ring via a deep NNE gap in gulick2019, and with blocked/slow refill in bahlburg2010.

parameters.label: Czas przejścia fali cofającej się przez całą Zatokę (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: 'within 10 h'; Brazos and Mimbral exposed (drawdown) after ~10 h, followed by the rushing wave.

parameters.label: Wysokość fali uderzającej w wybrzeże Ameryki Płn. (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: 'more than 200 m' (lower bound), followed by oscillations with 1-2 h periodicity.

parameters.label: Okres oscylacji po odbiciu fal w Zatoce (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: 'periodicity of 1-2 h'.

parameters.label: Średni wbieg fali na ląd wokół Zatoki (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: 'in excess of 150 m' (lower bound). No global model (incl. range2022) computed runup.

parameters.label: Maksymalny wbieg (zatoka Rio Grande) (Matsui 2002)
Zasięg zalania lądu (dolina Missisipi) (Matsui 2002)
parameters.notes: 'more than 300 km' (lower bound).

parameters.label: Przyjęta prędkość megatsunami (Sanford 2016)
parameters.method: scaling: maximum tsunami speed in 6 km water (Ward 2011 as cited)
parameters.notes: sqrt(9.81*6000) = 243 m/s. Upper-bound speed: real Gulf depths (1-4 km, shelves <200 m) make arrivals later.

parameters.label: Przybycie tsunami do skarpy Campeche (210 km)
parameters.notes: 14 min.

disagreements.topic: Dominant tsunami-generating mechanism (rim wave vs crater collapse / resurge 'rushing' wave)

positions.claim: The outward rim wave formed by the ejecta curtain carries most of the tsunami energy; a 'Crater Only' (collapse) run has ~13x less energy at 4 h.
Water flow into and out of the crater cavity causes most of the tsunami; the rim wave (~10 m at platform edge) disperses quickly and is negligible at the coast.

disagreements.assessment: Range et al. 2022 has more support: it couples a resolved hydrocode (100 m cells, 1-3 km water) to two independent global shallow-water models and tests the collapse-only case directly. Matsui's rim-wave estimate came from lab scaling for a wave forming over a 200 m-deep platform. The real answer is direction-dependent: north of the crater (water >=1 km) the rim-wave case applies; over the shallow S/SW platform, rim-wave generation is weaker, which axisymmetric models cannot capture. Treat as resolved in favour of the rim wave for far-field propagation, but contested near the source.

disagreements.topic: Did the ocean resurge rapidly into the crater (and form a collapse wave)?

positions.claim: Ocean resurge through a ~2 km-deep NNE gap flooded the crater up to the peak ring within 30-60 min, depositing ~80 m of sorted suevite within hours.
An ejecta/rim wall up to 200 m above sea level blocked forceful resurge and a collapse wave; refill was slow (0.18-1.5 m/s currents) by permeation through the wall.
Takes an 8 h crater-fill time over a 200 m-deep platform.

disagreements.assessment: Gulick et al. 2019 rest on direct peak-ring cores (M0077) and newer seismic bathymetry, so they have more support for fast resurge at least through the NNE gap. Bahlburg et al. analysed Yaxcopoil-1 in the SW sector, where a higher rim is plausible. Both can hold regionally (asymmetric target). For far-field tsunami energy the issue is minor: range2022 found similar energies with and without a sediment rim.

disagreements.topic: Arrival time of the first tsunami at the Gulf of Mexico margins

positions.claim: ~75-76 min to paleo-Florida/Texas coasts (distance at 0.25 km/s); megatsunami 'within 1-2 h'.
The tsunami reached the northern shelf about an hour after the Rayleigh waves (~5 min); the modelled tsunami leaves the Gulf for the Atlantic after ~1 h.
Rim-wave tsunami trains reached the far side of the Gulf 2-3 h after impact (citing Sanford et al. 2016).
The (crater-generated) receding wave crossed the Gulf within 10 h; the main rushing wave arrives after the drawdown.

disagreements.assessment: Mostly definitional. Deep-water arrival at the shelf break is ~1 h (deep-water speed ~200 m/s). Reaching the shoreline across broad shelves (c ~30-45 m/s at 100-200 m depth) can add 1-2 h, which reconciles 1 h with 2-3 h. Note that gulick2019's '2-3 h' is not what sanford2016 Table 3 gives. Matsui's 10 h applies only to his crater-dominated generation scenario, which newer work does not support. An eikonal solver on a paleobathymetry grid should settle this for the simulation; report shelf-break and shoreline arrivals separately.

disagreements.topic: Origin and timing of the Brazos River (Texas) event bed

positions.claim: Single sandstone bed from a tsunami ~50-100 m high, directly below the Ir anomaly and the K-Pg boundary.
High-energy debris flows and turbidites from multiple sources, probably multiple tsunami (or tempestites) plus reworking; ejecta at the base tie it to the K-Pg boundary.
A series of separate storm events with burrowed surfaces between them; the Chicxulub ejecta predate the K-T boundary by ~300 kyr.

disagreements.assessment: The impact-coincident event deposit (tsunami and/or gravity flows) has much stronger support: the 41-author synthesis in schulte2010 and later Gulf-wide mapping (sanford2016, kinsland2021) agree. The storm/pre-boundary interpretation is a minority position but has not been withdrawn; goto2005 reviews the debate. Treat Brazos as tsunami-influenced, with the inferred 50-100 m height as an order-of-magnitude hydraulic inference.

disagreements.topic: Is the shallow-water (non-dispersive) description adequate for the far field?

positions.claim: Long wavelength (50-100 km) makes shallow-water theory valid. Dispersion may cut amplitudes by up to 50% locally (undular bores), but the far-field pattern and energy directivity should change little, so shallow-water results are an upper bound.
The rim wave is strongly dispersive in deep water (Ursell number ~0.1) and decays quickly, leaving no measurable leading wave at the coast.

disagreements.assessment: Unresolved. Range et al. hand off at 600 s with a 50-100 km wavelength, for which dispersion is weak. Matsui assumed a much shorter-wavelength rim wave born in shallow water. Treat far-field amplitudes as upper bounds, with up to about 50% uncertainty. No published Boussinesq or 3-D global run for Chicxulub was found.

disagreements.topic: Late Cretaceous sea level (controls shelf width, coastlines and seaways in the paleobathymetry)

positions.claim: About 170 (85-270) m above present, from ocean-basin reconstructions.
About 40 m above present, from New Jersey margin stratigraphy (as summarised in Muller et al. 2008, who attribute the gap to dynamic subsidence).

disagreements.assessment: Muller et al. reconcile the two through mantle-driven subsidence of New Jersey, which favours the higher eustatic value used in the range2022 grid. Coastline positions remain uncertain by tens to hundreds of km on low-relief margins.

Excluded (not peer-reviewed): Ward, S. (2012, 2021) Chicxulub tsunami animations on YouTube, cited by range2022 as earlier Gulf-scale simulations. No peer-reviewed regional successor was found in this search.

Range et al. 2022 SI internal inconsistency: the Fig. S4 caption gives the fiducial initial energy as 5.1e19 J, but Table S4, the 0.19% efficiency, the 30,000x ratio and the Fig. S4 curve all imply ~5.1e20 J. This thread uses 5.1e20 J and flags the caption as a likely typo. Also: main text '1.5-km-high' wave at 10 min vs SI '1.4 km' (1.2 km with truncated mesh).

Oblique impact effect on the tsunami: Collins et al. 2020 put the trajectory at 45-60 deg from the NE. Range et al. expect a larger rim wave downrange (i.e. toward the SW, onto the shallow platform/Mexico) and smaller uprange (toward the deep Gulf/Atlantic), but this is not quantified. No 3-D oblique impact tsunami simulation for Chicxulub was found (speculation).

Rim-wave generation over the shallow S/SW Yucatan platform (water tens to ~200 m) vs the >=1 km-deep N/NE sector is not resolved by axisymmetric models; the azimuthal amplitude pattern of the source is unknown.

Air-pressure (Lamb-wave) driven tsunami: Range et al. (Sec. 5.4) argue it could be significant in the far field and would arrive earlier than the gravity-wave tsunami (Lamb wave ~300 m/s, cf. leveque2024 'slightly subsonic speeds (300 m/s or less)'), by analogy with Hunga Tonga 2022. Not modelled for Chicxulub in any verified source.

Landslide/slope-failure tsunamis around the Gulf (margins collapsed within minutes per sanford2016/denne2013/bralower1998) are not in the global model. matsui2002 found a modest landslide wave for a 140 x 75 km, 100 m-thick slide, but a much larger one if 10x thicker. Size and timing are unconstrained.

Paleobathymetry uncertainties that directly control eikonal arrival times: the depth and width of the Central American Seaway at 66 Ma (the range2022 grid has a broad, deep opening giving Pacific entry at ~4 h); whether the Western Interior Seaway was connected to the Gulf (leveque2024: unknown); shelf widths around the Gulf (sea level 85-270 m above present per muller2008); the Atlantic width and the mid-ocean ridge position (range2022 used Muller 2008 65 Ma age-depth plus the Scotese 70 Ma PaleoDEM, smoothed with a Blackman filter).

No verified global model computes runup or inundation. The only Gulf-wide runup numbers (mean >150 m, max 300 m, >300 km inland; matsui2002) come from a 2002 scenario whose generation mechanism is now disputed.

Range et al. 2022 hiatus-model correlation (91% incomplete sections where modelled flow >20 cm/s) is supportive but non-unique. Alternative causes of hiatuses on bathymetric highs are acknowledged by the authors.

Gulick et al. 2019 attribute '2-3 h' Gulf crossing to Sanford et al. 2016, whose Table 3 actually gives 75-76 min to the coasts. The discrepancy is unexplained; probably a shelf-crossing vs deep-water distinction.
Kinsland et al. 2025 paleo-slope depth '95-170 m (300-850 ft)' is internally inconsistent (850 ft = 259 m); the full text was not available to resolve it.

Recommended calibration data (not downloaded; ask the user before fetching): Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/GWOFIO (CC0) has the range2022 pre-impact paleobathymetry at 1/10 deg (tarball ~62 MB) and MOST_max_output.nc (~74 MB, maximum amplitude/velocity). These would let the eikonal solver use the same grid and calibrate heights cell by cell.
